move: multiply-blended discs, bars and serif word drift through each other on sines
how: On a paper ground, three large multiply-blended discs (red, blue, yellow), a teal horizontal bar and a pink vertical bar, plus two copies of the serif word 'Multiply', one upright in near-black and one italic in blue, both multiply-blended. No timeline: seek(t) maps t to a phase over 2pi and sets every transform as a sine or cosine of it: the discs drift 200 to 300px in x and 60 to 120px in y while breathing 10 to 15% in scale, the bars slide 220 to 240px and rotate plus or minus 14 to 18deg with a scaleX/scaleY breath, and the two words counter-drift x 40 / y 12 in opposite phase. Where shapes overlap, the multiply blend stacks their colours like ink. Every value is periodic in the 8s so the last frame returns to the first.
adapt: Change the word (and whether it is doubled), the five shape colours, sizes and starting positions, the paper tint and the captions; amplitudes can scale with the frame. Keep everything as sines of the phase so the loop stays seamless.
port: mount(el, shot) creates the five .s shapes, the two .t words and captions inside el; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline holding one proxy tween {p: 0 to 1, duration D, ease 'none'} whose onUpdate runs the gsap.set calls with phase p*2pi on targets resolved once from el.
caveats: seven multiply-blended layers over most of the frame are moderately expensive to composite
the fx.register seek loop must become an onUpdate proxy tween on the returned timeline
no entry or exit: it is a pure ambient loop
